clue.text: Bower is covering earl in shade

indicators.note: one thing covering another hides it, so the first word sits over the spot where the second was and takes its place

parts.note: violet is a shade of purple
E is the abbreviation for earl
taken as written

explanation.surface: A garden arbour shelters a nobleman in its shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bower' looks like a leafy shelter, which suits the shade, but here it is one who bows: a string player. IS replaces the E of VIOLET.
explanation.definitionFit: A violist plays the viola with a bow, so whimsically counts as a bower.

clue.text: Queen from the south supporting what Catullus wrote for sex capital

indicators.note: in a down entry a supporting part sits underneath, so it comes after the other part

parts.note: sex is Latin for six, which a Roman poet would write as the numeral VI

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading from the south means reading upwards from the bottom

parts.note: Queen Anne, British monarch

explanation.surface: A queen backs a Latin poet's erotic verse for a racy capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sex' is not about sex: it is the Latin word for six, and Catullus was a Roman poet, so he wrote it VI.
explanation.definitionFit: Vienna is the capital city of Austria.

clue.text: Most of fruit you reportedly bake in the sun for ape

indicators.note: most of something is all but a bit, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: an orange is a citrus fruit

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we want a letter that sounds like the word

parts.note: the letter U is pronounced like you
to tan is to darken the skin by lying in sunshine

explanation.surface: A recipe for an ape: take fruit and bake yourself in the sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: The orang-utan is a great ape of Borneo and Sumatra.

clue.text: Place inside popular painted flats?

parts.note: something popular is in fashion, or in
a theatre set is made from flats, painted wooden panels; the question mark flags this definition by example

explanation.surface: Someone is arranging popular painted apartments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flats' suggests apartments, but on stage flats are painted scenery panels that make up the set.
explanation.definitionFit: To inset something is to fit or put it into something else.

clue.text: Appropriate children disagree

parts.note: to appropriate is to take for oneself
issue is a legal word for offspring

explanation.surface: Children who are suitable fall out with each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' reads as the adjective suitable; it is the verb, to seize.
explanation.definitionFit: To take issue with someone is an idiom for disputing or objecting to what they say.

clue.text: Safe area for city's peculiar dialect

indicators.note: something peculiar is odd and out of the ordinary, so the letters are put into an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A city's odd local speech is treated as a protected zone.
explanation.definitionFit: A citadel is a fortress guarding a city, a stronghold where people can retreat in safety.

clue.text: Hint to capture rook against deviating line

indicators.note: capturing something means holding it, so the first word surrounds what follows

parts.note: a cue is a prompt or hint
R is the chess abbreviation for rook
V is short for versus, against

explanation.surface: A chess tip on capturing a rook versus a line of play that strays.
explanation.definitionFit: A curve is a line that bends away from straight.

clue.text: Used three wheels to move directly around the speed of light

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the next item
making the letters move shifts them into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
c is the physics symbol for the speed of light

explanation.surface: Someone rode three wheels straight round at light speed.
explanation.definitionFit: To tricycle is to ride a three-wheeled cycle, so the past tense means rode on three wheels.

clue.text: Trouble and strife originating in Amsterdam

definitions.meaning: first meaning: rhyming slang for wife

explanation.surface: Turmoil and conflict that started in Amsterdam.
explanation.walkthrough: Trouble and strife is Cockney rhyming slang for wife, and 'my old Dutch' is another Cockney term for a wife.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney slang one's Dutch is one's wife, and Dutch also means coming from the Netherlands.

clue.text: Check this out — new president-elect informally addressed city

parts.note: lo is an old word for look, see
N is the abbreviation for new
Don is a familiar short form of Donald, as in Donald Trump, president-elect when the puzzle appeared

explanation.surface: Look at this: the newly elected president gave a casual speech in a city.
explanation.definitionFit: London is the capital city of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Engineering vehicle's original handle for George Eliot

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for engineering
a van is a vehicle; with the apostrophe dropped, the possessive gives the S

explanation.surface: An engineering vehicle's first badge, named after the novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handle' is slang for name; George Eliot was a pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot was the pen name of Mary Ann Evans, so her real surname was her original name.

clue.text: Ethnic region mostly Turkish — and fractured

indicators.note: something fractured is broken into pieces that can be put back in another order
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A region whose people are largely Turkish, and divided.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, much of the region lies inside Turkey, and its partition is a political fracture.
explanation.definitionFit: Kurdistan is the region inhabited by the Kurdish people, spread across Turkey, Iraq, Iran and Syria.

clue.text: Clubs bats?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: evening entertainment such as nightclubs
second meaning, flagged by the question mark: creatures active after dark

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like sports equipment, clubs and bats, but one is the evening scene and the other nocturnal animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightclubs make up the evening entertainment scene, while bats are creatures that live by dark: life of the night.

clue.text: The oaf inside many a hoodlum

indicators.note: inside means the letters are tucked within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the boundary between the words

explanation.surface: The lout is at the heart of many a gangster.
explanation.walkthrough: Yahoos are the brutish humans in Gulliver's Travels, hence 'The'.
explanation.definitionFit: A yahoo is a coarse, boorish person, from the brutes in Swift's satire.

clue.text: Bishop leaving Letters to the Corinthians for others

indicators.note: when something is leaving it departs, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: Corinth was Greek, so letters to its people are Greek letters, here a pair of the second one
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop leaves St Paul's Epistles to the Corinthians for others to read.
explanation.walkthrough: The Epistles are a false path; Letters to Corinthians are Greek letters, and once the B goes, what is left are other Greek letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet, another letter from the beta.

clue.text: Obstruct progress? As well not, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged some other way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Should we block the advance? Maybe better not.
explanation.definitionFit: To stonewall is to block or delay by refusing to cooperate or answer.

clue.text: This is meant to arrest one returning from Mediterranean island

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, inserted to say a quoted error is meant

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so these letters are read the other way

parts.note: to nail a criminal is to catch them
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A police order to detain a man coming back from a Mediterranean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sic' is the note editors put in a quotation to show an oddity is deliberate: thus it was meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Sicilian means from or belonging to Sicily, the large island at the toe of Italy.

clue.text: About time to replace a knight in continuously changing list

indicators.note: to replace something is to take its place, so one letter is swapped in for another

parts.note: c is short for circa, about
an analogue signal varies continuously, unlike a digital one in steps
N is the chess notation for knight
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A list that keeps changing, with time taking the place of a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'continuously changing' looks like an anagram signal, but it defines a word: analogue, as opposed to digital.
explanation.definitionFit: A catalogue is a systematic list of items, such as goods for sale or books in a library.

clue.text: Country motorists touring American trail — one left going the wrong way

indicators.text: one left going the wrong way
indicators.note: the Roman one and the abbreviation for left already sit side by side in the word, and going the wrong way swaps them round
touring a place means going all around it, so the first part surrounds the rest

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, the UK motoring organisation
US is short for American
taken as written

explanation.surface: Drivers on a road trip across an American trail, but one turns left the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one left going the wrong way' adds no letters: I (one) and L (left) are already inside the trail, so the instruction reverses them in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia is a country, the only one that is also a whole continent.

clue.text: Near Portsmouth, where fish could be fresh

parts.note: the fish are in the water, so this gives the position word
the Solent is the strait between Portsmouth and the Isle of Wight

explanation.surface: Near Portsmouth is the spot where fish might be freshly caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' looks like it describes fish, but it means cheeky. The Solent is the stretch of sea off Portsmouth on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh in the sense of impudent or forward is a close synonym of rude and disrespectful.

clue.text: Occasionally admits husband's a looker

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Now and then she confesses that her husband is handsome.
explanation.definitionFit: Dish is informal slang for an attractive person, someone good-looking.

clue.text: Golf range's risky move

parts.note: Golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ambit means scope or range

explanation.surface: Playing on the driving range is a risky move for a golfer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Golf range' suggests a driving range, but the words split.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambit is an opening move in chess, or any calculated move, that risks something to gain an advantage.

clue.text: Islay still can make this stop

definitions.meaning: first meaning: whisky from Scotland; Islay is a Hebridean island famous for distilleries and a still is distilling apparatus
second meaning: to put an end to a rumour or plan

explanation.surface: An island distillery can still produce something that halts things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like the adverb yet; it is the copper pot of a distillery.
explanation.definitionFit: Islay distilleries produce Scotch whisky, and to scotch a plan means to put an end to it.

clue.text: Involved in prank levitating part of a pin over a foot

definitions.text: part of a pin over a foot

indicators.note: involved in means caught up within, so the letters are found within the next words

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A floating trick about part of a sewing pin and some distance.
explanation.walkthrough: Pins is old slang for legs, and the foot is the body part, not a unit of length.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle joint is the part of the leg just above the foot, and pin is informal for leg.

clue.text: Rulers' reservations after expression of disapproval

definitions.note: the clue's apostrophe-s is read as is

indicators.note: what is left after something is taken away is the remainder once it has gone

parts.note: bookings are reservations
a boo is a jeer of disapproval

explanation.surface: Monarchs' doubts follow a grumble of disapproval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reservations' reads as doubts but means bookings; 'after' means after the jeer has been taken off.
explanation.definitionFit: Kings are monarchs, those who rule a country.

clue.text: According to legend, people originally lived outside Rome in catacombs

parts.note: folk are people

indicators.note: originally points to how things begin, so only the opening letter of each word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: Legend has it that early Christians lived outside Rome in underground tombs.
explanation.definitionFit: Folkloric describes what belongs to folklore, the traditional stories and legends of a people.

clue.text: Sozzled American buddy forgetting name

indicators.note: forgetting something leaves it out, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: buddy is an American word for a friend
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A drunken American pal can't recall someone's name.
explanation.walkthrough: Sozzled is British slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Fried is slang for drunk or intoxicated, like many cooking words.

clue.text: Organ player ultimately wrong to be upset

indicators.note: something upset is turned over, which in a down entry flips the letters to read upwards
ultimately means in the end, so just the last letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter
evil means morally wrong

explanation.surface: An organist finally gets it wrong and is distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ player' wants to be a musician; the organ is the definition and the player gives only its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The liver is an internal organ of the body that cleans the blood.

clue.text: Musicians, becoming increasingly geriatric, wrapping up

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
aging means growing older

explanation.surface: Elderly musicians are finishing their final tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrapping up' suggests finishing; it means binding a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: Bandaging is binding a wound with a strip of cloth, literally wrapping it up.

clue.text: One who'll perhaps fold — very feeble, losing pawn to gain tempo

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very

indicators.note: losing something means parting with it, so that letter disappears

parts.note: pale can mean weak or feeble, as in a pale imitation
P is the chess abbreviation for pawn
T is the abbreviation for tempo

explanation.surface: A weak chess or poker player gives up a pawn to gain a tempo, then folds.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess and poker vocabulary misleads: the valet folds his master's clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A valet is a personal manservant who looks after clothes, so he might fold them.

clue.text: Fought ex-PM, ignoring resistance — she did this for 44 days

indicators.note: ignoring something means leaving it out of account, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: Liz Truss, briefly UK Prime Minister in 2022
R is the physics symbol for resistance
she led the country for 44 days before resigning

explanation.surface: A former prime minister fought on, ignoring opposition, during her short spell in office.
explanation.walkthrough: Liz Truss was the UK's shortest-serving Prime Minister, in office for about 44 days in 2022.
explanation.definitionFit: Tussled is the past tense of tussle, to scuffle or struggle with someone, so it means fought.

clue.text: Disregarded extremely mean Republican party harangue

indicators.note: with its extremes disregarded, the word loses its outermost letters

parts.note: near is an old word for stingy, mean with money
R is short for Republican
a bash is a party

explanation.surface: A mean Republican party ignored, haranguing them.
explanation.walkthrough: Earbash is Australian slang for talking at someone at length.
explanation.definitionFit: To earbash is to talk incessantly at someone, lecturing or nagging them, as a harangue does.
